html:
SMTO-HTTP-0052 — The Gateway's web request feature isn't working

GUID: b836c11a-e07b-402c-82d3-f9f2b3555ba4
Slug: http-gateway-runtime-error
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The Gateway on the selected computer hit an internal problem while preparing or handling a web request, so SMTO didn't get a result.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, find the Gateway this task used, select Check for updates and install any update offered. An update replaces the Gateway's web request software, which is the part that failed.
  2. If that doesn't help, ask the person who manages that computer to run the SMTO Gateway installer again there, then restart the Gateway once no tasks are running on it. Reinstalling repairs damaged parts of the Gateway while keeping its pairing and settings.
  3. If the earlier step was changing something on another service, first check that service to see whether the change already happened. Then start a new task and ask the Agent for the web request again. Checking first avoids making the same change twice, and a new task picks up the repaired Gateway.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows Connected and a web request in a new task returns a result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't delete the Gateway, its pairing or saved sign-ins, and don't re-enter the website's password or key; the problem is the Gateway's software, not your sign-in.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The selected Gateway's native HTTP runtime failed its readiness check (a mandatory HTTP module failed to import for a reason other than a missing package) or raised an unexpected local exception while processing the request.

What this means

  • Native HTTP initialization failed, or request processing raised an unexpected exception outside the transport exception classes. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Native HTTP initialization failed, or request processing raised an unexpected exception outside the transport exception classes.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish readiness/import failure from an exception after dispatch and retain attempted/effect_unknown facts.

How to fix it

  • On the Gateway host, run python -m gateway_core.http_runtime in the Gateway's environment and read the Gateway log for the exception. If the installation is at fault, rerun the matching installer as the Gateway's account, restart the Gateway once its active jobs are settled and refresh its capabilities; otherwise keep the log for defect diagnosis and reconcile any write that may already have been sent.
  • Inspect the Gateway failure phase. Repair proven installation problems; otherwise retain the occurrence for runtime defect diagnosis and reconcile possible effects.
  • After an installation repair: After active jobs and uncertain operations are reconciled, restart the affected Gateway. Restart the server too if the shared installer updated it. Refresh Gateway metadata before starting a new task.

Retry and execution caution

  • Confirm the reported capability works on the selected Gateway after correcting its diagnosed cause. If installation repair was needed, require the installer checks to pass. Refresh metadata and start a new task when capabilities change; existing tasks keep their captured snapshot. Inspect prior execution receipts before repeating work.

How to verify the fix

  • Initialization and a bounded read work; any earlier possible mutation has been reconciled.

What not to do

  • Do not enter target API credentials to repair a missing Gateway dependency.
  • Do not restart a Gateway with unsettled mutations without first reconciling its active work.
  • Repair the installation in place; do not delete Gateway pairing, credentials, settings, browser profiles or task artifacts.
  • Granting a Skill permission does not install its dependencies.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
